mcqs.q: What is the relationship between atman and Brahman in Hindu philosophy?
options: Nirvana is the name of a Buddhist god.
Atman is the body and Brahman is the soul.

Atman is the individual self/soul; Brahman is ultimate reality. In Advaita Vedanta, atman IS Brahman — the self is identical with ultimate reality, and liberation comes from realising this non-duality.
Atman and Brahman are two competing Hindu gods.
Nirvana is the Buddhist version of heaven.
Act utilitarianism is about action movies and rule utilitarianism is about laws.
The 'blowing out' of the fires of craving, hatred and delusion — liberation from the cycle of rebirth (samsara), not a heavenly afterlife.
Nirvana is the name of a Buddhist god.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between act and rule utilitarianism?
options: Act utilitarianism is about action movies and rule utilitarianism is about laws.

Act utilitarianism judges each individual action by its consequences; rule utilitarianism follows rules that, if generally adopted, would produce the most good — sacrificing case-by-case calculation for predictability and fairness.
Nirvana is the name of a Buddhist god.
Act and rule utilitarianism are basically the same approach.
